agents.label: AI agents
agents.description: What an agent should be allowed to do, how it proves the work is done and where it fits in work your team already runs.

mcp.label: MCP
mcp.description: Connecting assistants to products and services through the Model Context Protocol: scoped tools, checked access and results you can inspect.

webmcp.label: WebMCP
webmcp.description: Actions a web page exposes to a browser agent, so the person and the agent work from the same state.

voice.label: Voice
voice.description: Spoken instructions that end in a result you can inspect, from a dashboard that reports back to directing work across apps.

accessibility.label: Accessibility
accessibility.description: Whether people can finish the job, whichever way they reach the interface, and how to measure the whole journey.

ui.label: UI
ui.description: How interfaces decide what people must learn, and what changes when an agent can act on the page.

operations.label: Operations
operations.description: Daily briefs, dashboards and the decisions they feed: evidence first, then a person decides.

permissions.label: Permissions
permissions.description: Authority, boundaries and read-back for delegated work: the place in the code that enforces what an agent may do.

skills.label: Agent skills
skills.description: Specialist knowledge recorded so an agent can use it again: sources, accepted examples, checks and stopping points.

databricks.label: Databricks
databricks.description: Lakebase, AppKit and portable AI engineering choices on the Databricks platform.

databases.label: Databases
databases.description: Modelling agent state: managed Postgres against document stores, and the transactions each one supports.

streaming.label: Streaming
streaming.description: Server-sent events and the contracts between the agent runtime, the application and the browser.
